title: s+consonant → es-, ser: soy, es, son, somos, eres; ¿cómo es?

cards.title: st-, sp-, sc- → est-, esp-, esc-
cards.body: Spanish words can't begin with s + consonant, so related words gain an e: state ↔ estar.

cards.title: ser: el humano vs el ser humano
cards.body: Humano is a noun in el humano and an adjective (after the noun) in el ser humano.

cards.title: soy = I am (ser)
cards.body: Only four verbs end in -oy for 'I': voy, doy, estoy, soy. Your occupation is a characteristic, so it takes ser.

cards.title: es, son → somos (working backwards)
cards.body: From son (they are), swap the they ending for the we ending: somos.

cards.title: eres = you are (informal)
cards.body: The oddest form; link it to es.

cards.title: ser in full
cards.body: Ustedes is just 'you guys' almost everywhere: it doesn't sound formal in the plural (except in parts of Spain).

examples.en: I am · he/she is · they are · you all are · we are · you are
examples.es: yo soy · él/ella es · ellos son · ustedes son · nosotros somos · tú eres

cards.title: ¿Cómo está? vs ¿Cómo es?
cards.body: ¿Cómo está? asks about someone's state (how are they doing). ¿Cómo es? asks about their characteristics (what are they like).
